subject: Biotechnology
title: Defining Biotechnology
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Defining Biotechnology.

hook.text: Humans used living organisms as tools for 10,000 years — biotechnology is older than writing itself.

buildup.text: At its core, biotech means using biology to make useful products — from bread to insulin.

discovery.text: Modern biotech adds precision — we now edit genes, engineer cells, and design proteins on purpose.

twist.text: The term biotechnology was coined in 1919 by a Hungarian engineer — not a biologist.

climax.text: Today biotech spans medicine, agriculture, industry, and energy — one of the broadest fields.

punchline.text: Biology is technology — the oldest kind and the newest.

quiz.question: What does biotechnology fundamentally mean?
options: Using computers to simulate biological processes
Using living organisms or their components to make useful products

details.summary: Biotechnology is the use of living organisms, cells, or biological systems to develop products and technologies that benefit humanity. It spans ancient practices like fermentation to modern applications including gene editing, therapeutic protein production, and environmental remediation.
details.whyItMatters: Biotechnology touches every aspect of modern life from medicine and food to energy and materials. Understanding its scope and definition helps navigate an industry projected to exceed one trillion dollars in global revenue.
takeaways: Biotechnology uses living systems to create products benefiting humanity
It ranges from ancient fermentation to cutting-edge gene editing
Applications span medicine, agriculture, industry, and the environment

faq.question: What is the simplest definition of biotechnology?
faq.answer: Using living things to make useful products. This covers everything from yeast making bread to engineered bacteria producing insulin. The UN Convention on Biological Diversity defines it as any technological application using biological systems or living organisms.

faq.question: How large is the global biotechnology industry?
faq.answer: The global biotechnology market is valued at over 800 billion dollars and is projected to exceed one trillion by 2030. It employs millions worldwide across pharmaceuticals, agriculture, industrial manufacturing, and environmental services.
